bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical fragmentation and energy-supply disruption — The global economy remains susceptible to renewed trade disruptions and geopolitical escalations; escalating tensions in West Asia could disrupt key energy supply routes and trigger volatility in global oil markets, impacting fuel prices, logistics costs and industrial production.
- Tightening emission and safety regulation and evolving EV policy — The industry operates in a dynamic regulatory environment characterised by tightening emission and safety norms and evolving fuel efficiency and Electric Vehicle policies, which drive product re-engineering and compliance investment.
- Supply chain constraints and rising compliance costs — Explicitly flagged by the Board as a challenge for the industry alongside the regulatory environment, affecting input availability and cost.
- Demand-side pressure from affordability and financing conditions — The Board flags affordability and financing conditions as demand-side pressures; volume growth in FY 2025-26 was itself partly a function of the September 2025 GST rate rationalisation lowering cost of ownership, making demand sensitive to policy support.
- Intensifying competition in the auto component landscape — The competitive landscape is intensifying with global OEM participation, new EV entrants and increasing focus on technology, localisation and innovation.
- Overseas / European exposure — A significant minority share of consolidated total income is generated by overseas operations, and European auto sales grew only modestly (about 1.8% year-on-year in FY 2025-26), so Europe remains a slower-growth, macro-exposed part of the portfolio.
- Concentration on a major OEM customer — New business wins from OEMs in India are reported excluding orders from one of the Company's major OEM customers, indicating a single customer relationship large enough to be disclosed separately.
- Technology transition risk from electrification — Accelerating EV adoption, ADAS advancement and record BEV market shares in advanced markets are reshaping the components industry, requiring continuous reinvestment to keep the ICE-linked portfolio relevant.

- The Government's draft guideline extending ABS requirements to lower-capacity two-wheelers reinforces a shift the Company is already positioned for, with rising customer preference for safety
- Raw material costs, particularly aluminium alloy which accounts for about 55% of purchases, experienced inflationary pressure, making margin management a priority
- Escalating Middle East geopolitical conflict disrupted shipping routes and triggered an energy crisis that pushed up fuel and power costs and strained availability and pricing of critical raw materials, showing up directly in input costs

- One-time costs during the year related to strategic consulting initiatives, aftermarket expansion and the initial ramp-up of new greenfield plants
- European operating landscape expected to remain complex in the near term, shaped by the transition to electric and hybrid vehicles, evolving EV policy timelines, rising competition from Chinese OEMs and macroeconomic pressures
- India-EU Free Trade Agreement and the India-US interim trade framework expected to open new avenues for domestic manufacturers, with quota-based auto liberalisation allowing EU automakers into higher price segments in India
- Industry demand backdrop: two-wheeler sales grew 12.9% year-on-year in FY 2025-26 with scooters up 18.6%, total four-wheeler sales rose 10% and three-wheelers expanded by nearly 24%
- Indian EV retail sales rose 24.6% YoY to 24.5 lakh units in FY 2025-26, outpacing the broader automobile market

- The lithium-ion battery pack facility near Pune has already secured a confirmed order from a leading two-wheeler EV OEM
- Inverted front fork platform adoption rose to six OEMs, including a new programme that entered production during the year, with further opportunities under validation

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Endurance Technologies Limited manufactures a diversified portfolio of automotive components encompassing aluminium die casting and machining, suspension systems, braking systems (including disc brakes and ABS), transmission components, alloy wheels and embedded electronics such as ABS ECUs and Battery Management Systems. It serves major Indian and global OEMs across the two-wheeler, three-wheeler and four-wheeler segments from strategically located plants in India and Europe, and is extending into electric-mobility components such as lithium-ion battery packs and into non-automotive applications including niche components for solar power generation plants. The business is supported by five DSIR-approved R&D centres and next-generation Suspension and Brakes R&D facilities focused on proprietary technologies.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Premiumisation in the two-wheeler market continues to support demand for inverted front forks, assist-and-slip clutches and hydraulic braking systems
- September 2025 GST rate rationalisation on auto components improved vehicle affordability and supported a pickup in sales that extended well beyond the typical festive season
- The Government's draft guideline extending ABS requirements to lower-capacity two-wheelers reinforces a shift the Company is already positioned for, with rising customer preference for safety
- Raw material costs, particularly aluminium alloy which accounts for about 55% of purchases, experienced inflationary pressure, making margin management a priority
- Escalating Middle East geopolitical conflict disrupted shipping routes and triggered an energy crisis that pushed up fuel and power costs and strained availability and pricing of critical raw materials, showing up directly in input costs
- The Company absorbed part of the steep, conflict-driven cost increases to support vendors ahead of recovering them from OEM customers
- The four greenfield plants will see significant ramp-up in FY 2026-27, with the full impact of these investments on revenues and profitability expected during the year
- One-time costs during the year related to strategic consulting initiatives, aftermarket expansion and the initial ramp-up of new greenfield plants
- European operating landscape expected to remain complex in the near term, shaped by the transition to electric and hybrid vehicles, evolving EV policy timelines, rising competition from Chinese OEMs and macroeconomic pressures
- India-EU Free Trade Agreement and the India-US interim trade framework expected to open new avenues for domestic manufacturers, with quota-based auto liberalisation allowing EU automakers into higher price segments in India
- Industry demand backdrop: two-wheeler sales grew 12.9% year-on-year in FY 2025-26 with scooters up 18.6%, total four-wheeler sales rose 10% and three-wheelers expanded by nearly 24%
- Indian EV retail sales rose 24.6% YoY to 24.5 lakh units in FY 2025-26, outpacing the broader automobile market
- Global auto components industry projected to reach $ 609.34 billion in CY 2026 and $ 896.71 billion by CY 2032 at a 6.58% CAGR, powered by electrification and autonomous technologies
- The alloy wheel plant at AURIC Bidkin commenced production in October 2025 with its entire capacity of 3.6 million units per annum already booked
- The lithium-ion battery pack facility near Pune has already secured a confirmed order from a leading two-wheeler EV OEM
- Inverted front fork platform adoption rose to six OEMs, including a new programme that entered production during the year, with further opportunities under validation
- Solar damper business emerged as a promising new vertical with supplies initiated from the Pantnagar plant to a Spanish client
- Aftermarket reach spans India through a distributor network and extends to nearly 40 countries across Asia, Africa and Latin America

capex_expansion.body: The Company continued to make progress on its greenfield and expansion projects during FY 2025-26. In October 2025 production commenced at the AURIC Bidkin plant in Dist. Chh. Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra, for alloy wheels, with an installed capacity of 3.6 million wheels per annum. It is poised to commence production at its AURIC Shendra plant in Dist. Chh. Sambhajinagar for the manufacture of machined aluminium castings catering to four-wheelers and non-automotive applications. A lithium-ion battery pack plant is being set up at Mindewadi in Pune, Maharashtra, to cater to growing demand from EV and energy storage applications. In addition, the Company is establishing new capacities across various locations for braking systems, ABS and electronics, while also setting up a new aluminium forging facility to support increasing customer demand. themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
